v.why: Extra convs show diminishing returns when another output-side edge is already a strong conv.
A strong direct conv path already saturates capacity, so the added conv gains less.
A parallel strong conv into the output reduces the marginal gain of this one.
When the final edge is already a strong conv, upgrading the node-2 branch gains less.
With a strong conv at the input edge, upgrading the inner edge has diminishing returns.
A strong direct conv path makes an additional 1x1 conv on edge 5 less valuable.
Removing the direct edge hurts more when edge 4 is also absent, since few paths to the output remain.
Cutting a strong input conv is far more damaging than cutting a weak one.
Strong parents lose more when the edge is degraded to none.
Removing a strong 3x3 conv loses more than removing a weak op.
